rekening.intro: Your measurements set against large studies. No made-up personal prediction — but the direction is clear.
rekening.teWeinig: After {n} days of sleep or step data, you'll see here what your habits cost you. Connect Health Connect on your Android phone and it happens automatically, or track your sleep and steps yourself.

stappen.jij: You usually walk about {stappen} steps a day.
stappen.goedUitleg: lower risk of premature death, per 1,000 steps a day
stappen.goedOnderzoek: You're in the zone where the risk levels off in research. Every extra 1,000 steps a day was linked to a 15% lower risk of premature death — and no upper limit has been found yet. This is an association in large groups, not a guarantee.
stappen.tekortUitleg: steps a day short of the {zone} where the risk levels off
stappen.tekortOnderzoek: Every extra 1,000 steps a day was linked to a 15% lower risk of premature death. In an American model, the least active quarter of over-40s lived up to almost 11 years less than the most active quarter. Associations in large groups — not a personal prediction, but a clear direction.
stappen.stap: That's about {minuten} extra minutes of walking a day.

slaap.goedUitleg: longer life for men with five healthy sleep habits (women: 2.4 years)
slaap.goedOnderzoek: You're getting your 7 hours — one of the five habits in this study. The other four: falling asleep quickly, sleeping through, no sleeping pills and waking up rested. Preliminary research and an association, not proof of cause.
slaap.tekortUitleg: shorter life for men with at most one of five healthy sleep habits (women: 2.4 years)
slaap.tekortOnderzoek: People who slept 7–8 hours and had the other four habits (falling asleep quickly, sleeping through, no sleeping pills, waking up rested) lived longer on average than those with at most one. Right now you're missing the first. Preliminary research and an association, not proof of cause.
slaap.stap: You're {tekort} short of 7 hours. Start by going to bed {minuten} minutes earlier.

vo2max.jij: Your VO2max (fitness) is {waarde}. In this study, that falls in the "{groep}" group.
vo2max.uitleg: lower risk of premature death per 3.5 points higher VO2max
vo2max.onderzoek: Fitness is one of the strongest predictors we know of. Across 33 studies, every 3.5 points higher VO2max was linked to a 13% lower risk of premature death. Below {laag}, that research calls your fitness low; from {hoog}, high. An association in large groups, not a personal prediction.
vo2max.stap: You're {tekort} points below "high". Brisk walking, cycling or running at a pace where you can barely talk, a few times a week, is what raises your fitness.

rusthartslag.jij: Your resting heart rate is usually {n} beats per minute.
rusthartslag.uitleg: higher risk of premature death per 10 beats higher resting heart rate
rusthartslag.goedOnderzoek: You're below 60, the lowest-risk group in this study. Above that, risk rose by about 9% per 10 beats, even within what doctors call "normal". An association, not proof that lowering it extends your life.
rusthartslag.tekortOnderzoek: Across 46 studies, the risk of premature death rose by about 9% per 10 beats higher resting heart rate, even within what doctors call "normal" (60–100). Above 80, the risk was 45% higher than in the lowest group. An association, not proof that lowering it extends your life.
rusthartslag.stap: For most people, regular endurance training and enough sleep go hand in hand with a lower resting heart rate. If it suddenly shoots up or you don't feel well, talk to your GP.
